answer: Each answer carries a proof-of-work stamp at 21 bits of difficulty, and the stamp is bound to the identity so it cannot be computed once and shared. Because the anchor stamp is verified against the thread nonce, the grove audit can check it and a recycled stamp fails the binding. A farm as a result pays the hashing cost per key per epoch, which is a linear compute bill rather than a one-off build. Honest users pay that once, farms 36 times. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
